newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia 97 platinum metals exports seen down on 96.
newsitem.headline: Russia 97 platinum metals exports seen down on 96.

text.p: Russia's platinum and palladium exports in 1997 will be down on 1996 levels because of extended delays to resuming shipments, a top official at Russian precious metals export agency Almazjuvelirexport said on Tuesday.

"It could be that they (1997 deliveries) are somewhat lower (than last year) because half the year has gone by already," Sergei Gorny, deputy director of the agency, told Reuters. "I can't exactly say how much they will be in figures, but I don't think they will be as low as half."

Gorny said recent talks with clients in Japan, the world's biggest consumer of platinum group metals (PGMs), had ended satisfactorily and there would be no further delays in deliveries from Russia, which supplies 60 percent of the world's palladium and 20 percent of its platinum. But he declined to give delivery dates.

"We will work according to the deals we have concluded -- we are known for carrying out our job reliably," he said. "If we signed a deal for July 3, for example, we would start to deliver on July 3. I can't say exactly when the first deliveries will be, but there will be no delays and everything is fine."
Gorny said Almaz would not supply any more platinum or palladium than was "necessary" and said it would fulfil contracted volumes before supplying non-contracted metals.

Palladium prices recently hit 17-year highs, with platinum hitting a seven-year high, largely on delays in deliveries from Russia. Russian officials have cited bureaucratic delays and changes in the structure of the precious metals markets as the main reasons for the delays. But Almaz has given widely differing comments on the nature of the delays and what volumes would be.
